Lemma
[Properties of the cut locus]

↗ def:cut-locus ↗ def:cut-time-locus ↗ lem:segment-domain-star-shaped

Let $M$ be complete and connected, and let $p\in M$. Then:

  1. $U_p$ is an open, star-shaped neighborhood of $0$ in $T_pM$, and $d(p,\exp _p(w))=|w|$ for every $w\in U_p$;

  2. $\exp _p(U_p)$ is open and the cut locus ${\mathcal C}_p=M\setminus \exp _p(U_p)$ is closed;

  3. ${\mathcal C}_p$ has measure zero.

Proof

\sketch ↗ def:cut-locus ↗ lem:localized-cut-locus ↗ thm:hopf-rinow ↗ lem:normal-ball Radial minimality is downward closed, which proves star-shapedness. A finite cut time is attained by continuity of distance. If the endpoint were neither conjugate nor joined by a second minimizing geodesic, the inverse function theorem and compactness of minimizing initial vectors would extend uniqueness and minimality beyond the cut time, a contradiction. These arguments also give continuity of the cut time along directions where the alternatives remain separated.

□
